# Quantum Unit initial authoring context

Copyright 2026 Masahiko G. Yamada. SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0.

This is informed authoring under adopted #27/#43, not blind model evaluation.
The author had read the common type tree, finite Unit phase regressions, selected
CLI profile checks, sized projection and native hierarchy port representation.
The exact deployed model identifier and sampling settings were not recorded.

The six desired sources use existing grammar with an exact Q<Unit> basis that
the sized projection currently rejects. Op<Unit> applies the already-defined
Op<Bit>/Op<Bits<n>> provider/control syntax to that desired basis; it is not
reported as implemented. The six deliberate counterexamples preserve distinct
Unit/Bits0 types and linear zero-width ownership. Two current controls separate
ordinary Unit copy from a quantum Bits0 owner. No new unit/finish spelling,
implicit cast, source-access contract, primitive semantics or native rule is
adopted by this packet. Physical width zero means a one-dimensional Hilbert
space, not absence of a quantum owner or scalar action.

Each complete project includes a nullary ordinary Unit main solely to permit
finite project checking. Selected checks target main::f; the finite check's
main artifact does not execute f, so a finite check is not a scalar semantic
execution or a proof about the selected open function. Earlier type/profile
rejections can mask deliberate downstream faults and must be reported as such.

Original source/Qargo bytes, expectations, binary/kernel and current source
identities are frozen before any observation. The existing CLI and kernel are
reused without rebuilding/copying either binary. Only bounded check commands
are planned (at most one quantum bit), not a build, maximum case, full replay,
new guarantee admission, issue completion or release validation. Future repairs
must use separately named attempts/derivatives; these first bytes stay fixed.
